Summary: [EDS-DA] Hero Carousel block - core build & decoration
Description:
As a developer, I need to build a Hero/Banner Carousel block for the Girl Scouts site (based on the Figma 'Banner' component, node 5168-208528) so that authors can present rotating promotional slides on the homepage and landing pages.

Design reference: Desktop frame 1280x720, padding 60px 120px, flex column, justify space-between. Each slide has a full-bleed background image, an eyebrow line, a large serif heading, a primary outline button, a secondary text link with chevron, and an optional Terms & Conditions link bottom-right.

Approach: Adapt the Block Collection Carousel (/block-collection/carousel) for slide navigation/structure and reuse the local hero block's slide content/overlay styling. Do NOT build carousel mechanics from scratch.

Tasks:
- Create blocks/carousel/carousel.js and carousel.css (or hero-carousel variant)
- Decorate each slide row into a slide with background image + content container
- Implement slide track, active-slide state, and transition
- Wire arrows and dots to navigation logic
Acceptance Criteria:
- Block renders one slide per authored row
- Background image is full-bleed; content overlays with readable contrast
- Eyebrow, heading, primary button, and secondary link render per slide
- Active slide visible; others hidden; smooth transition between slides
- No console errors; block decorates within eager/lazy phase appropriately
- Code passes npm run lint

Summary: [EDS-DA] Hero Carousel - DA authoring model & content structure
Description:
As a content author, I need a clear Document Authoring structure for the Hero Carousel so that I can create and edit slides in DA without developer help.

Authoring model (block table named 'Carousel' or 'Hero Carousel'): each slide = one table row. Suggested columns/structure per slide:
- Image cell (background image)
- Content cell containing: eyebrow text (plain line), heading (H1/H2), primary CTA (link styled as button), secondary CTA (link), optional Terms & Conditions link

Tasks:
- Define and document the exact table layout authors will use
- Document how eyebrow vs heading vs CTAs are distinguished (e.g., first line = eyebrow, heading = bold/H-level, links order = primary then secondary)
- Provide a sample DA document with 4 slides matching the Figma
- Document optional cells (Terms link) and graceful handling when omitted
Acceptance Criteria:
- Authoring structure documented with a visual example
- Sample DA doc renders correctly as a 4-slide carousel
- Omitting the secondary link or Terms link does not break layout
- Authors can add/remove/reorder slides by adding/removing rows
- Eyebrow, heading, and both CTAs map to the correct rendered elements

Description:
As a site visitor, I need to navigate between carousel slides using arrows and position indicators so that I can browse all promotional messages.

Design reference: circular left/right chevron arrows (vertically centered, GS green), and a row of 4 dots indicating slide position/active slide at bottom-center.

Tasks:
- Implement previous/next arrow controls
- Implement clickable slide-position dots reflecting active slide
- Implement looping behavior (wrap from last to first)
- Optional autoplay with configurable interval; pause on hover and on focus
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion (disable autoplay/transitions)
Acceptance Criteria:
- Arrows move to previous/next slide and loop correctly
- Dots reflect the active slide and are clickable to jump to a slide
- If autoplay enabled: pauses on hover and keyboard focus
- prefers-reduced-motion disables autoplay and reduces transitions
- Controls have visible, on-brand styling matching the Figma

Description:
As a site visitor on any device, I need the Hero Carousel to adapt across breakpoints so that content remains legible and usable.

Design reference: Desktop variant is 1280px wide, 720px tall, padding 60px 120px. Mobile/tablet variants exist in the Figma (GS_Responsive modes). Mobile-first CSS with min-width breakpoints at 600px / 900px / 1200px per project standards.

Tasks:
- Implement mobile-first layout; stack/scale content for small screens
- Reduce padding and heading size on mobile; ensure image focal point remains sensible
- Ensure arrows/dots are touch-friendly (>=44x44px targets) on mobile
- Verify no horizontal scroll at 320px and at 200%/400% zoom
Acceptance Criteria:
- Layout adapts cleanly at 375px, 768px, 1280px and 1440px
- Heading and padding scale down on mobile per design
- Touch targets for arrows/dots meet 44x44px minimum
- No horizontal scrolling at 320px viewport or at 400% zoom
- Background image remains visually balanced across breakpoints

Description:
As a user relying on assistive technology, I need the Hero Carousel to be fully accessible so that I can perceive and operate all slides and controls.

Aligns with the project WCAG 2.1 AA + Section 508 requirements.

Tasks:
- Add appropriate roles/labels (region with aria-label; group/aria-roledescription=carousel pattern)
- Make arrows and dots keyboard operable with visible focus indicators
- Provide accessible names for arrow buttons (Previous/Next slide) and dots (Go to slide N)
- Ensure background images have appropriate alt text; decorative images use empty alt
- Announce slide changes via aria-live (polite) without overwhelming AT
- Verify text-over-image contrast meets 4.5:1 (add overlay/scrim if needed)
Acceptance Criteria:
- Entire carousel operable by keyboard (Tab/Enter/Space/Arrow keys)
- Visible focus indicator on arrows and dots with >=3:1 contrast
- Arrow and dot controls have descriptive accessible names
- Slide changes announced via aria-live; no keyboard trap
- Text contrast over background image passes 4.5:1 (scrim applied if required)
- axe-core scan returns zero violations on a page with the block

Summary: [EDS-DA] Hero Carousel - slide content styling (eyebrow, heading, CTAs)
Description:
As a brand stakeholder, I need each slide styled to match the Girl Scouts visual design so that the carousel is on-brand.

Design reference: eyebrow in small caps/sans, heading in large serif (white), primary CTA as outline button (white border, transparent fill, uppercase label 'SHOP PRODUCTS'), secondary CTA as uppercase text link with right chevron ('EXPLORE MORE >'), optional 'Terms & Conditions*' link bottom-right on a subtle scrim.

Tasks:
- Apply GS design tokens (colors, typography, spacing) to slide elements
- Style primary button (outline) and secondary link (text + chevron) states: default/hover/focus
- Position Terms & Conditions link bottom-right
- Ensure content max-width and left alignment per design
Acceptance Criteria:
- Eyebrow, heading, and CTAs match Figma typography, color, and spacing
- Primary button renders as outline style with correct hover/focus states
- Secondary link shows chevron and correct hover/focus states
- Terms & Conditions link positioned bottom-right and legible
- Visual matches Figma at desktop within reasonable tolerance

Summary: [EDS-DA] Hero Carousel - QA, cross-browser & visual validation
Description:
As a QA engineer, I need to validate the Hero Carousel against the Figma design and across browsers so that it meets quality and brand standards before release.

Tasks:
- Compare rendered block against Figma 'Banner' component (node 5168-208528)
- Test in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge (latest)
- Test keyboard, screen reader (NVDA + VoiceOver), and zoom
- Validate authoring flow end-to-end in DA with a real sample document
- Log and triage any visual or functional defects
Acceptance Criteria:
- Rendered block matches Figma within agreed visual tolerance
- Functions correctly in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge
- Passes keyboard + screen reader + 200%/400% zoom checks
- Author can build/edit a 4-slide carousel in DA successfully
- Zero open Critical/Major defects at sign-off
